findings.summary: The sign-in return destination allows external redirects: LoginForm passes from directly to router.replace, and the form API accepts /\attacker.example/path as an external URL. See the cross-check report F1 for the real-login reproduction and source locations.

Five failed sign-ins at minutes 0, 3, 6, 9 and 12 do not enforce the promised fifteen-minute lockout: a correct password is accepted at minute 16, only four minutes after the fifth failure. The sliding-window count loses the first failure. See report F2.

The unrestricted local administrator is rejected by surviving cookie-shape authentication checks after the permission guard succeeds. Real loopback next dev requests without cookies return 401 from /api/admin/arquitectura and /api/taller/hoja-armado; a random syntactically valid cookie changes the former to 200. See report F3.

Deleting an account retains its personal email in sign_in_attempts when an unsuccessful sign-in preceded the invitation. deleteAccount removes attempts by account_id only, leaving the older account_id NULL row. See report F4 for the real PostgreSQL reproduction.

The sign-in endpoints accept cross-site form POSTs and issue session cookies without checking Origin or a CSRF token. An attacker with an invited account can log a victim's browser into that account. SameSite=Lax does not authenticate a login request that needs no existing session cookie. See report F5.

The production integration permission oracle reads expected permissions from production policy, probes protected routes only with GET, ignores method overrides and accepts 405 or 5xx for allowed APIs. It cannot establish the required independent role-by-method permission matrix. Separate proxy tests cover only a subset and do not repair this end-to-end gap. See report F6.
